the_negative_control_is_what_makes_the_P.description: A restore step that puts SOME file back would report success whether or not it checks which file. The whole value of a rehearsal is that it shows the guard refusing. Without X2, AC1 would be satisfied by a step that blindly copies.

the_negative_control_is_what_makes_the_P.expected_not_landed: the control passing because the step accepted a wrong copy, or the control not being exercised at all
the_negative_control_is_what_makes_the_P.observed: X2 NEGATIVE CONTROL: PASS -- a kept copy that is not st31's is refused before anything moves. The guard it exercises is the real arm's own: remove_st32_to_st31.sh refuses unless the kept library is st31's, and the order says that if it is ever run and cannot find that file at that digest it exits before moving anything and this seat reports that. the_order_was_HELD_and_was_not_run_until.description: THE CONTROL THAT GOVERNED THIS ORDER FOR AN HOUR. Its own text forbids running while TCKT_VNEXT's fifth run is between submission and close, and the order arrived minutes after this seat delivered the j4 baseline that authorises that run -- so the hold was almost certainly live on arrival. The failure mode is not subtle: running a host script during another seat's live run.
the_order_was_HELD_and_was_not_run_until.expected_landed: the script is not sent until the condition's OWNER says the run is closed; everything that does not depend on the condition is done meanwhile
the_order_was_HELD_and_was_not_run_until.expected_not_landed: inferring the condition from a reading that cannot carry it, in particular reading a 0/0/0 queue as proof the run had closed

THAT WAS NOT TREATED AS THE CONDITION, because an unsubmitted run and a closed run read identically and the baseline had just gone out, making unsubmitted the likelier. The order was parked with its owner and one line asked for. THE WORLD THEN SETTLED IT: at ~17:28Z the same queue read 0 visible / 1 IN FLIGHT, so a run was live on the host; had the 0/0/0 been read as closed, this script would have run during it. The release came at 18:03Z (msg 5523) on the issuer's own reading -- the job terminal ATTENTION at 17:24:48Z, and this seat's j5 read at 17:53:32Z showing 0 children and the queue at 0 and 0 -- and the script was sent at 18:08:07Z, after taking the step-1 gate again (0/0/0), which the release message said still comes first.

ONE assignment: line 13, H=$(mktemp -d /tmp/st32-rollback-dry.XXXXXX). Every write targets $H -- lines 14 and 15 (the two copies in), 19 (the install under test), 24 (the negative control's wrong copy) -- and line 26 is rm -rf $H.
